title: Dataset curation and captioning for training
hook: What core's training path really does with your pictures and captions, how often it sees each one, and why a caption decides what a trigger word learns.

verified.claim: A folder named N_something repeats its pictures N times. A missing caption becomes an empty string.
Every step draws torch.randperm(dataset)[:batch], so counts per picture vary, and none is guaranteed.
A caption beyond 75 tokens goes into another group of 77 rather than being cut: the real SD1Tokenizer gave 1, 1, 2, 2 and 3 groups for 10, 75, 76, 150 and 151 tokens.
Pictures of different shapes switch the trainer to a mode that processes them one at a time.
The caption checks we quote are those in the studio's Train page.
Groups are joined along the token axis: the real encode_token_weights with a stub encoder gave 1 x 154 x 768 for 76 tokens and 1 x 231 x 768 for 151.

unchecked: The caption toy is linear algebra on made-up numbers. It shows the mechanism, and a real model is much more complex. We did not train real LoRAs with different captions.
Advice on how many pictures to use, and on writing captions, is common practice. We have one run (CU-281) and it doesn't compare captions.
The draft's claim that a model fails on synonyms because of caption frequency was removed: we could not support it.
